newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans lower on exports, July liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans lower on exports, July liquidation.

text.p: CBOT soybeans were lower at midsession Thursday, with July under pressure from slow export sales and liquidation in the July contract, traders said.
"We're seeing a weaker tone in the July (soybeans) because of the exports," said one floor trader.
USDA Thursday said for the week ended June 19 net export sales of old crop U.S. soybeans totaled 9,200 tonnes. That figure came in far below expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
New crop export sales of 432,200 tonnes were near the high end of expectations for 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes and were considered slightly supportive to November, traders said.
Talk that a large commercial firm is planning to bring soybeans to Chicago to deliver against futures still ciruculated in the market and weighed on July.
First notice day is Monday. On that day, July will trade without limits and many traders anticipating volatile trade are exiting the contract.
In early trade, Smith Barney and Cargill Investor Services each sold one million bushels November, pit traders said.
At 1058 CDT, July soybeans were 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower at $8.12, and other months were 1/4 to two cents lower.
